source.title: From Perturbation Correction to Geometry-Aware Sampling: Sharpness-Guided Equilibrium Sampling for Balanced Flat Minima in Long-Tailed Learning

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper; no truncation or wrong-document issue is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates how SAM-based training and sampling choices change class-balanced test accuracy in long-tailed learning, refining claims about sharpness and generalization in a distinct setting.
record.gate_note: The study tests geometry-aware sampling and SAM variants on long-tailed classification benchmarks. It does not directly test memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, convolution versus fully connected architecture, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Cited findings about SAM or other methods are not this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The study uses sharpness-aware optimization to develop a sampler and reports its classification performance. It does not test any specified version. In particular, its SAM-induced loss-change proxy is not magnitude-aware sharpness, and it reports neither train-test gaps nor correlations or rankings of generalization measures required by V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that frequency- and sharpness-guided sampling improves medium- and tail-class performance under severe imbalance with little computational overhead, while requiring tuning of warm-up and sharpness feedback.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a geometry-aware sampling method for long-tailed learning rather than testing the claim's specified interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Warm-up ratio and sharpness exponent change reported accuracy; results also differ across imbalance ratios, datasets, loss settings, and fine-tuning protocols.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100 LT at IR100 with cross-entropy, SGS-SAM achieves 47.56% overall and 19.75% tail accuracy, versus reported Focal-SAM baselines of 44.0% and 8.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frequency- and sharpness-guided sampling can improve long-tailed classification accuracy, particularly for tail classes.

fits_no_version.finding: Warm-up ratio and sharpness exponent affect classification accuracy; gains also depend on imbalance and fine-tuning protocol.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benefits of geometry-aware sampling depend on sampling hyperparameters and the training setting.

record.problems: This work studies long-tailed balanced accuracy rather than the claim's stated natural-label generalization and train-test gap. Some comparisons in Table 5 are reported as results of cited methods, and Table 6 training-time comparisons are taken from Focal-SAM. The text describes theoretical bounds under assumptions; it does not report a direct measurement of generalization gap or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows for the specified claim versions: the paper's own results concern long-tailed classification accuracy and sampling-method comparisons, which the versions do not cover.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 classification conflicts with its otherwise correct finding that no version is tested. The conditional PAC-Bayes analysis does not establish V7's empirical correlation. Longer fine-tuning schedules do not test V5 because batch size is not varied. No qualifying result rows are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and its correlation with train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
